title: GTA 6 review: Eurogamer on a game with no single hook
description: GTA 6 review: Eurogamer says Rockstar's game is huge, detailed and built around Jason and Lucia's relationship, with cars at the centre. Here's the gist.

body.text: The first GTA 6 review from Eurogamer is out, and it argues that Rockstar's new game resists any one-line summary. The reviewer calls it enormous, richly detailed and full of contradictions, and says it is built around a relationship rather than just rampages. The excerpt we worked from doesn't include a final score, so we won't quote one.
What the GTA 6 review says about the game

The reviewer tried several ways to sum the game up. First came the idea that the car has become a modern American "third place", and in GTA 6 it does seem to be where a lot happens. According to Eurogamer, that's where you take calls that trigger missions, spend time with your partner, escape police and gangs, and discover much of the map. It's also a place to store weapons, disguises and stolen goods.

Then the reviewer dropped that theory as too narrow. The conclusion is that GTA 6 has no single thread to pull. It is vast but crammed with tiny detail, ridiculous but sometimes mature, tender and violent. Eurogamer says the game gives you an escape hatch when something annoys you, and it is not claiming perfection. There are nitpicks, though they fade when you step back.
Jason, Lucia and a story about love

Eurogamer keeps story details light to avoid spoilers. Jason and Lucia are on the run after a fetch quest goes wrong, and who is chasing them stays unclear early on. The publication notes that, despite leaks, Rockstar kept the story's beginning and ending secret.

The review stresses that this is a relationship story. You begin as Jason alone, waiting in his island hometown for Lucia to be released from prison. Your first to-do list is oddly ordinary: groceries, flowers, clothes for her, unfinished DIY jobs. Eurogamer says the result is far from dull and gives room for humour and character between bigger set pieces.

Performances get heavy praise. Lucia's actor, Manni L. Perez, is described as natural and charismatic, with a wide emotional range. Jason is the quieter counterpart, and the reviewer calls him a gentle, considerate lead. The relationship is built through small moments and debriefs after missions, and your earlier behaviour shapes how the other character responds.

Eurogamer says the game keeps nudging you to question your priorities: is this optional task worth it, and will the choice matter? Working out the systems is part of the fun, according to the reviewer.

items: You can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you want to ignore that side.
GTA 6 has a control overhaul, but old-style controls are offered from the first screen.
Optional missions, such as buying flowers early on, let you slow down before the action ramps up.

body.text: This is one outlet's view, and the reviewer admits the take may change as more of the game reveals itself over coming days and weeks. Watch for more reviews, player reactions to the relationship-first approach, and whether the control changes and optional systems land well with the wider community. Eurogamer's verdict is that GTA 6 won't suit everyone, but no game has tried harder to be everything.

faqs.q: Who are the main characters in GTA 6?
faqs.a: According to Eurogamer, the story begins with protagonists Jason and Lucia, who are on the run after a simple fetch quest goes wrong. Lucia is played by Manni L. Perez.

Eurogamer describes it as a story about a relationship and arguably the first blockbuster game to be so explicitly a love story. You can nurture or neglect that relationship, but it sits at the heart of the game.

faqs.q: Can you change the controls in GTA 6?
faqs.a: Yes. Eurogamer says the game has had a control overhaul, but you can switch to the old controls from the first screen you see.
